stem: During a consent discussion for a non-urgent procedure, a 16-year-old gives a clear answer when alone but changes position completely whenever one parent enters the room and cannot explain the change; which concern is most relevant when assessing competence?

options.text: Inability to manage influences on decision-making

explanation: Inability to manage influences on decision-making is the key concern. Competence for consent includes the ability to maintain and explain a decision despite pressure or external influence, so marked changes in position when a parent enters the room raise concern in this area.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because school performance is not a criterion for assessing competence to consent in this scenario.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because competence includes the ability to manage influences on decision-making, and a decision that changes under parental pressure suggests difficulty in this area.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because being under 18 years alone does not determine competence to consent.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because previous hospital admission is not part of the competence assessment described here.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because Medicare status is unrelated to competence to consent.
